title: Kafka Event Streaming: Topics, Consumers and Exactly-Once in Practice
concept: Move an order service to events with Kafka: topics and partitions, keys and ordering, consumer groups and rebalancing, offsets and retries, dead-letter topics, idempotent producers and the outbox pattern. Challenges are TypeScript consumers and producers graded against an in-memory broker.
description: Move an order service to events with Kafka: topics and partitions, keys and ordering, consumer groups and rebalancing, offsets and retries, dead-letter topics, idempotent producers and the outbox pattern. Challenges are TypeScript consumers and producers graded against an in-memory broker. 7 lessons, each applying the tool to a real production situation, with 1-2 graded challenges per lesson.

learningOutcomes.text: Choose topics, partition counts and message keys so related events stay in order.
Produce without losing or duplicating events: acks, idempotent producers and the transactional outbox.
Run consumer groups that survive rebalances, commit offsets after the work and park poison messages.
Change event schemas without breaking the consumers that read them.

knownIssues: Challenges run TypeScript against an in-memory broker that follows Kafka's documented semantics (partitions, offsets, groups, idempotence), not a real cluster.
testedVersions are not yet re-checked against a live cluster.

lessons.title: Committing offsets after the work, not before
